subject.title: Context poisoning via session transcript reinjection — agents loop after reading their own/other agents' looping transcripts

question: Should OpenClaw make loop detection safer by default and add a context-boundary sanitizer for repeated transcript blocks, or keep the current opt-in detector while first collecting a narrower reproducible failure case?
rationale: The report combines a configuration-default change with new behavior for compaction and transcript-reading paths; source and docs show adjacent safeguards but do not define the acceptable false-positive policy for legitimate repeated work or diagnostic transcript access.

options.title: Stage a bounded core safeguard
options.body: Add a narrowly measured repeated-call/repeated-text guard at model-context assembly, preserve original transcript data, and evaluate a default change only with fresh-install and upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep detection opt-in for now
options.body: Document fresh-session recovery and collect a redacted current-main reproduction that identifies the specific read and compaction path before changing defaults.

options.title: Route only the policy to a plugin seam
options.body: Expose a typed context-sanitization hook and leave default policy to plugins, accepting that core users remain unprotected until an extension is installed.

recommendation.title: Stage a bounded core safeguard
recommendation.body: Add a narrowly measured repeated-call/repeated-text guard at model-context assembly, preserve original transcript data, and evaluate a default change only with fresh-install and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The available feature-history signal is closest to the existing loop-detection implementation that any default-policy decision would extend.
